data.name: Ghamay
data.gender_notes: Ghamay is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Ghamay means 'delight' or 'pleasure'. It is derived from the root word 'ghama', which means 'to delight' or 'to please'. This name is rich in spiritual significance and is often used to describe the feeling of being in the presence of Allah (swt) or experiencing His blessings. The name Ghamay carries the meaning “Delight, Pleasure” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghamay usually hope their child will grow to embody delight, pleasure and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the pleasure and happiness found in the remembrance of Allah
data.etymology: Ghamay belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Delight, Pleasure.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghamay total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Ghamay was a famous market in the medieval Islamic city of Fustat (old Cairo), Egypt. It was particularly known for selling exotic animals, birds, and perfumes.

Ghamay was also a popular caravan stop and waystation on the trans-Saharan trade routes during the 13th to 16th centuries CE. Merchants from as far as the Sudan and the Sahel traded gold, ivory, and slaves for textiles and other goods.
